correctness.rationale: For every n≥2, r in [1,n−1], and q≥1, the reachable columns are coordinate vectors, so rank is the number of covered coordinates. Missing coordinate s is exactly the pair of extreme independent binomial events C_s=q and C_{s−r}=0 (probability 4^(−q)). Their joint-event conflict graph is g cycles of length n/g, including K2 for order-two offset; expanding the PGF gives the exact cycle independence polynomial. The independent-set count, quadratic recurrence, q=1 specialization, bounded-degree factorial-moment Poisson limit, and Var(X)≤EX high-mean bound have complete analytical proofs with stated quantifiers. A standalone, standard-library exact-rational enumerator reproduces the full rank-deficiency law in 74 distinct parameter cases and validates selected roots. Finite verification is not substituted for the all-n proof.

value.rationale: The motivating 2024 pointwise-sparse control paper treats rank loss as a central feasibility hazard and motivates guaranteed algorithms, but gives no exact estimate for unguided sampling. The exact all-parameter deficiency distribution quantifies that hazard, showing exponentially small success at the shortest feasible horizon for coprime offsets and a sharp logarithmic-repetition Poisson recovery transition. The gcd dependence separates arithmetic geometry of actuator placement from the asymptotic onset; the result is a natural, motivated benchmark for independently sampled actuator schedules, not an arbitrary finite slice. The theorem is deliberately restricted to two channels, cyclic shifts and uniform independent choices, so no claimed significance for rank-aware MCMC performance.
